title: pipelines.chromake.scripts.paths
text:
pipelines.chromake.scripts.paths
The paths module of chromake contains functions to identify the inputs and the files generated by the chromake pipeline.





Name
Description




get_all_frip_output
Get all project-level FRIP output files.


get_all_multicov_output
Get the files necessary for the multicov rules of a project.


get_all_project_peaks
Get the files necessary for the peak calling rules of all projects.


get_all_sequencings_related_paths
Get the path to the files generated by the pipeline for the samples of all sequencings and projects.


get_project_paths_for_frip
Get the files necessary to compute FRiP for all samples of a project.


get_project_paths_for_macs
Get the files necessary for the macs2/macs3 rules of a project.


get_project_paths_for_multicov
Get the files necessary for the multicov rule of a project.


get_sequencings_related_paths
Get the path to the files generated by the pipeline for the samples of a specific sequencing.

title: pipelines.chromake.scripts.config
text:
pipelines.chromake.scripts.config
The config module of chromake contains functions to read and write the config file of the chromake pipeline.





Name
Description




check_config_format
Check the configuration file to make sure it follow the requirements of chromake. At runtile, it will stop snakemake if the file format is invalid.


check_project_and_sequencing
Remove empty sequencing entries and update PROJECTS so that each project


check_sample_files_exist
Check if all R1 and R2 FASTQ files listed in the config exist.


create_config_from_table
Create a YAML config from a table. Supports SAMPLES and optional INPUT files.


create_example_config
Create an example genomake/chromake YAML configuration file.


create_samplesheet_from_config
Create a samplesheet table (CSV or Excel) from a YAML config, resolving relative paths


remove_samples
Remove specific samples from a project in the YAML config.


remove_sequencing
Remove an entire sequencing project from the YAML config.


update_jobs
Update or add the JOBS section in an existing YAML config.

pipelines.chromake.scripts.config.update_jobs(config_path, jobs)
Update or add the JOBS section in an existing YAML config.
CORES_PER_JOBS: number of cpu cores to use for each jobs (>=1)
SCHEDULER_PROFILES: if using an executor like slurm, indicate the name of the qos (e.g. short), and the associated MaxWall in minutes.











Name
Type
Description
Default




config_path
str
Path to the YAML config file.
required


jobs
dict
Dictionary containing JOBS information to update. Can be a full replacement or partial update.
required






jobs_update = {
    "CORES_PER_JOBS": {
        "FASTQC": 10,
        "CUTADAPT": 10,
        "BOWTIE2": 30,
        "SAMTOOLS_QC": 5,
        "MULTIBAMSUMMARY": 5,
        "BEDTOOLS": 5
    },
    "SCHEDULER_PROFILES": {
        "default": {"qos_name": "short", "partition_name": "standard"}, # default value
        "short": {"MaxWall": 24 * 60, "qos_name": "short", "partition_name": "standard"}, # 1 day
        "medium": {"MaxWall": 3 * 24 * 60, "qos_name": "medium", "partition_name": "standard"}, # 3 days
        "long": {"MaxWall": 8 * 24 * 60, "qos_name": "long", "partition_name": "standard"}, # 8 days in minutes
    }
}
update_jobs("config.yaml", jobs_update)

title: Get started
text:
The genomake package is a collections of scripts and pipeline written in python to analyze with genomic data.
This package is a WIP.

title: Get started
text:
Objectives
The chromake pipeline is a pipeline to analyze ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, H3K27me3, and H2Aub marks), and ATAC-seq samples. It use fastq samples to:

Realize an optional adaptor trimming (cutadapt)
Align samples to a genome reference using bowtie2
Identify enriched peaks (macs3)
Realize quality controls (fastqc, samtools stats, samtools flagstat, multiqc)

This pipeline is a WIP. It currently performs QC, optional adapter trimming, alignment, filtering of non-standard chromosomes, generation of UCSC-compatible tracks, MACS peak calling, project-level count matrices, and FRiP calculation. Secondary analysis such as PCA, differential analysis, and gene ontology may be added at a later date.

title: Get started
text:
Configuration file
Chromake is configured with a YAML file passed to Snakemake through the genomake chromake -c argument. The file is loaded by Snakemake as the config object and checked at runtime by chromake.scripts.config.check_config_format().
A complete config has three top-level sections:

SEQUENCINGS: required. Describes each sequencing run or sequencing folder, the FASTQ files, the optional input controls, the trimming parameters, and the genome-dependent resources used by the rules.
PROJECTS: optional for FASTQ alignment but required for peak calling and project-level analyses. It groups samples from one or several sequencings by assay/mark and defines the project output directory.
JOBS: optional but recommended. It controls the number of threads used by each rule and, when using a cluster executor such as Slurm, maps requested runtimes to scheduler partitions and QoS names.







ImportantAbout the SEQUENCINGS section (important)






A sequencing should only list samples from a same sequencing run. It can list samples from different experiment (e.g. H3K27ac ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq).
You may need to split a sequencing in two or more parts if:

you configure chromake to realize an adapter trimming with cutadapt, and the samples you sequenced on a single run need to be trimmed for different adapter sequences.
your samples don’t use the same input sample for the peak calling. It is possible to add multiple samples in the INPUT subsection but only the first one will be used during the peak calling step.






Check the config example template
The fastest way to start is to create the example YAML file and edit it manually:
from genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts import config as chr_config

chr_config.create_example_config("config.yaml")
Then edit config.yaml to replace the example sample names, FASTQ paths, genome references, blacklist file, chromosome-size file, project paths, and Slurm settings with values for your analysis.


Minimal YAML structure
The YAML file uses arbitrary names for sequencings, projects, samples, and input controls. In this example, MO203 is a sequencing name, H3K27ac_BAP1 is a biological sample, and Input_Batch1 is the input control used for ChIP-seq peak calling.
SEQUENCINGS:
  MO203:
    PATH: "/scratch/my_project/MO203/"
    R1_ADAPTOR: "AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA"
    R2_ADAPTOR: "AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT"
    SAMPLES:
      H3K27ac_BAP1:
        R1: "FASTQ/H3K27ac_BAP1_R1.fastq.gz"
        R2: "FASTQ/H3K27ac_BAP1_R2.fastq.gz"
        TYPE: "H3K27AC"
      ATAC_BAP1:
        R1: "FASTQ/ATAC_BAP1_R1.fastq.gz"
        R2: "FASTQ/ATAC_BAP1_R2.fastq.gz"
        TYPE: "ATAC"
    INPUT:
      Input_Batch1:
        R1: "FASTQ/Input_Batch1_R1.fastq.gz"
        R2: "FASTQ/Input_Batch1_R2.fastq.gz"
    PARAMETERS:
      CUTADAPT: "-q 20 --pair-filter=any"
      BOWTIE2_REF: "/path/to/bowtie2/index/genome"
      GENOME: "hg38"
      BLACKLIST_BED: "/path/to/hg38-blacklist.v2.bed"
      CHROM_SIZE: "/path/to/hg38.chrom.sizes"

PROJECTS:
  ChIP_H3K27AC:
    SEQUENCINGS: ["MO203"]
    TYPE: "H3K27AC"
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 1
    PROJECT_PATH: "/scratch/my_project/ChIP_H3K27AC/"
  ATAC:
    SEQUENCINGS: ["MO203"]
    TYPE: "ATAC"
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 1
    PROJECT_PATH: "/scratch/my_project/ATAC/"

JOBS:
  CORES_PER_JOBS:
    FASTQC: 10
    CUTADAPT: 10
    BOWTIE2: 30
    SAMTOOLS_QC: 5
    MULTIBAMSUMMARY: 5
    BEDTOOLS: 5
  SCHEDULER_PROFILES:
    default:
      qos_name: "short"
      partition_name: "standard"
    short:
      MaxWall: 1440       # 1 day, in minutes
      qos_name: "short"
      partition_name: "standard"
    medium:
      MaxWall: 4320       # 3 days, in minutes
      qos_name: "medium"
      partition_name: "standard"
    long:
      MaxWall: 11520      # 8 days, in minutes
      qos_name: "long"
      partition_name: "standard"


SEQUENCINGS section
Each entry under SEQUENCINGS represents one sequencing batch or one folder containing FASTQ files and pipeline outputs.








Field
Required
Description




PATH
yes
Root directory for the sequencing. Relative R1 and R2 FASTQ paths are interpreted from this directory. Chromake also writes sequencing-level outputs here, including BAM, BED, BEDGRAPH, HOMER, QC, and TRIMMED.


SAMPLES
yes for normal analyses
Dictionary of biological samples. Each sample must contain R1, R2, and TYPE.


SAMPLES:<sample>:R1
yes
Path to the read 1 FASTQ file. Prefer a path relative to PATH, for example FASTQ/sample_R1.fastq.gz.


SAMPLES:<sample>:R2
yes
Path to the read 2 FASTQ file. Prefer a path relative to PATH.


SAMPLES:<sample>:TYPE
yes
Assay or mark analyzed for that sample. Valid values are ATAC, H3K27AC, H3K27ME3, and H2AUB.


INPUT
required for ChIP-seq peak calling
Dictionary of input/control FASTQ files. It uses the same R1/R2 format as SAMPLES, but does not need a TYPE. ATAC-seq projects do not need INPUT. If several inputs are listed, all are processed, but only the first input is used for MACS peak calling.


R1_ADAPTOR, R2_ADAPTOR
optional
Adapter sequences passed to cutadapt. If both are present and non-empty, trimming is performed before alignment. Set both to an empty string, or omit them, to align the raw FASTQ files directly.


PARAMETERS
yes
Sequencing-specific rule parameters. See the table below.



The PARAMETERS sub-section contains genome and tool options:








Field
Required
Description




CUTADAPT
optional
Extra cutadapt arguments, for example -q 20 --pair-filter=any. If missing, chromake adds a default empty string.


BOWTIE2_REF
yes
Bowtie2 index prefix used for alignment. Give the prefix expected by bowtie2 -x, not a FASTA file unless that is how your wrapper expects it.


GENOME
yes
Genome passed to HOMER. This can be a HOMER genome name such as hg38/mm10 if configured in HOMER, or a genome FASTA path depending on your HOMER setup.


BLACKLIST_BED
yes
BED file of blacklisted regions to remove after alignment.


CHROM_SIZE
yes
Chromosome-size file used when creating genome browser tracks.





PROJECTS section
Projects define which aligned samples are pooled for peak calling and project-level quantification. A project does not list sample names directly. Instead, it lists sequencing names and a TYPE; chromake selects all samples from those sequencings whose sample TYPE matches the project TYPE.








Field
Required
Description




SEQUENCINGS
yes
List of sequencing names defined under the top-level SEQUENCINGS section.


TYPE
yes
Project assay/mark. Must be one of ATAC, H3K27AC, H3K27ME3, or H2AUB. Only samples with the same TYPE are used in the project.


MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS
optional
Minimum number of samples in which a peak must be found to be retained in the merged project peak set. If missing, chromake defaults to 1.


PROJECT_PATH
yes
Output directory for project-level files, including MACS peaks, merged peaks, count matrices, and FRiP results. Use a different path for each project.



For ChIP-seq projects (H3K27AC, H3K27ME3, H2AUB), the associated sequencing must contain at least one INPUT entry. For ATAC-seq projects, no input control is required.


JOBS section
JOBS controls resources requested by Snakemake rules.








Field
Required
Description




CORES_PER_JOBS
optional
Number of threads used by each rule family. Missing values are filled with chromake defaults. Recognized keys are FASTQC, CUTADAPT, BOWTIE2, SAMTOOLS_QC, MULTIBAMSUMMARY, and BEDTOOLS.


SCHEDULER_PROFILES
optional
Runtime-to-scheduler mapping used when launching Snakemake with an executor such as Slurm. It is ignored for local runs.


SCHEDULER_PROFILES:<tier>:MaxWall
yes for non-default tiers
Maximum runtime for that tier, in minutes. Chromake selects the smallest tier whose MaxWall is greater than or equal to the runtime requested by the rule.


SCHEDULER_PROFILES:<tier>:qos_name
yes
QoS name passed to the scheduler resource field.


SCHEDULER_PROFILES:<tier>:partition_name
yes
Partition name passed to the scheduler resource field.



The default tier is used as a fallback. It does not need MaxWall, but it must contain qos_name and partition_name if you use cluster resources.


Create a config from a sample sheet
A second workflow is to describe samples in a table and convert it to YAML with create_config_from_table(). This is useful when sample metadata are already maintained in Excel or CSV.
The long-format sample sheet must contain these columns:







Column
Description




SAMPLE
Sample or input-control name.


SEQUENCINGS
Sequencing name. Must match a key in the sequencings argument passed to create_config_from_table().


PROJECT
Project name for biological samples, or exactly INPUT for input controls.


TYPE
Assay/mark for biological samples. Use ATAC, H3K27AC, H3K27ME3, or H2AUB. Leave empty for INPUT rows.


STRAND
R1 or R2. Use one row per FASTQ mate.


PATH
FASTQ path. Absolute paths are converted to paths relative to the corresponding sequencing PATH when possible.



Example table:











SAMPLE
SEQUENCINGS
PROJECT
TYPE
STRAND
PATH




H3K27ac_BAP1
MO203
ChIP_H3K27AC
H3K27AC
R1
/scratch/my_project/MO203/FASTQ/H3K27ac_BAP1_R1.fastq.gz

MO203
ChIP_H3K27AC
H3K27AC
R2
/scratch/my_project/MO203/FASTQ/H3K27ac_BAP1_R2.fastq.gz


Input_Batch1
MO203
INPUT

R1
/scratch/my_project/MO203/FASTQ/Input_Batch1_R1.fastq.gz


Input_Batch1
MO203
INPUT

/scratch/my_project/MO203/FASTQ/Input_Batch1_R2.fastq.gz



Conversion example:
from genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts import config as chr_config

chr_config.create_config_from_table(
    table_path="samplesheet.xlsx",
    output_path="config.yaml",
    proj_paths={
        "ChIP_H3K27AC": "/scratch/my_project/ChIP_H3K27AC/",
        "ATAC": "/scratch/my_project/ATAC/",
    },
    jobs={
        "CORES_PER_JOBS": {
            "FASTQC": 10,
            "CUTADAPT": 10,
            "BOWTIE2": 30,
            "SAMTOOLS_QC": 5,
            "MULTIBAMSUMMARY": 5,
            "BEDTOOLS": 5,
        },
        "SCHEDULER_PROFILES": {
            "default": {"qos_name": "short", "partition_name": "standard"},
            "short": {"MaxWall": 24 * 60, "qos_name": "short", "partition_name": "standard"},
            "medium": {"MaxWall": 3 * 24 * 60, "qos_name": "medium", "partition_name": "standard"},
            "long": {"MaxWall": 8 * 24 * 60, "qos_name": "long", "partition_name": "standard"},
        },
    },
    sequencings={
        "MO203": {
            "PATH": "/scratch/my_project/MO203/",
            "R1_ADAPTOR": "AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA",
            "R2_ADAPTOR": "AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT",
            "PARAMETERS": {
                "CUTADAPT": "-q 20 --pair-filter=any",
                "BOWTIE2_REF": "/path/to/bowtie2/index/genome",
                "GENOME": "hg38",
                "BLACKLIST_BED": "/path/to/hg38-blacklist.v2.bed",
                "CHROM_SIZE": "/path/to/hg38.chrom.sizes",
            },
        },
    },
)
You can also export a YAML config back to a sample sheet:
chr_config.create_samplesheet_from_config(
    config_path="config.yaml",
    output_path="samplesheet.xlsx",
    strand_columns=False,
    excel=True,
)

section: Validate a config before launching Snakemake
text:
Validate a config before launching Snakemake
Before running the full pipeline, validate both the config structure and the input FASTQ paths:
import yaml
from genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts import config as chr_config

with open("config.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(stream)

chr_config.check_config_format(cfg, raise_error=False)
chr_config.check_sample_files_exist("config.yaml")
Use raise_error=True to stop immediately on invalid mandatory fields. This is the default behavior used at runtime by the Snakefile.

title: Get started
text:
Launching the pipeline
Once the configuration file is created, chromake can be launched using the CLI included in genomake:
genomake chromake -c ./config.yaml --cores 250 --jobs 10
If you need to:

use an executor
do a dry run
unlock the directory

Then you can use the --others-snakemake argument. Here an example for the slurm executor:
genomake chromake -c ./config.yaml --cores 250 --local-cores 1 --jobs 8 \
   --others-snakemake "--executor slurm --default-resources \
   slurm_account=<your_slurm_account> clusters=<name_cluster_for_computation> --slurm-logdir \
   ./logs --slurm-keep-successful-logs --slurm-delete-logfiles-older-than 0 \
   --rerun-incomplete"
You can check the final command without launching it using the -p argument of genomake chromake.






NoteAbout executor (note)






You may replace the slurm executor by another if you don’t work with slurm.
Please visit the slurm executor documentation for more information about how to use it.

title: Get started
text:
Outputs
The outputs of chromake will be placed in the directories of the sequencings (trimmed fastq, qc, bam, bedGraph track) or the directories of the projects (bed resulting from the peak calling).
Sequencing:

BAM: bam files resulting from the alignment and their index. Two versions are kept. The one outputed by bowtie 2 and a version trimmed (the pipeline only keep the standard chromosome) and sorted.
BED: bed files generated by bedtools genomecov using the sorted bam files.
BEDGRAPH: folder contening the begGraph file for UCSC visualization
HOMER: folder generated by homer makeTagDirectory
QC: results of various qc (fastqc and multiqc, cutadapt logs, bowtie logs, samtools flagstat, samtools stats, size of the fragments)
TRIMMED: trimmed fastq path

text:
pipelines.chromake
Chromake pipeline
Chromake is used to align sequencing data of ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq experiments, identify peaks, and realize a read count. All those steps are realized using a snakemake pipeline included in this subpackage.


The ressources used can be modified. In particular, the number of cores can be specified in the config file while other ressources (memory, runtime) will necessite to copy and modify the snakefile included in this subpackage.
Chromake contains submodules (genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts.config and genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts.paths). Among them, paths is used by the snakefile to track the files it generate, while config was created to help the user create the YAML config file needed by snakemake.



To run the pipeline:

you need at least 60 Go of RAM.

To install the necessary programs. It can be done with conda using a file like:

name: genomake
channels:
  - bioconda
  - conda-forge
  - anaconda
dependencies:
  - bedtools
  - bowtie2
  - fastqc
  - homer
  - openssl
  - picard
  - python
  - ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig
  - ucsc-bedtobigbed
  - samtools
  - pip:
      - git+https://github.com/Pierre9344/genomake
      - MACS3 # can be modified to MACS2 and the pipeline will detect which version to call in the rule
      - cutadapt
      - deeptools
      - multiqc
      - snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm

you need a configuration file in a yaml format. Check genomake.pipelines.chromake.scripts.config.create_example_config for an example. The config submodule contains functions to generate such a config file from a samplesheet.
The configuration is composed of 3 main fields:

SEQUENCINGS
PROJECTS
JOBS


SEQUENCINGS is used to define the sample of a sequencing run that share similar adapter for trimming the reads, genome reference, and input samples (for ChIP-seq, more than one input can be indicated but only the first one will be used when identifying peak).
Each sequencing must have a parameters field to indicates at least: - the genome reference for bowtie2 (BOWTIE2_REF) - a bed of blacklisted regions (BLACKLIST_BED), see https://github.com/Boyle-Lab/Blacklist to download the file corresponding to the genome you use - a file indicating the chromosome size (CHROM_SIZE), see https://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/goldenpath/hg38/bigZips/ to download the one for GRCh38/hg38. UCSC also host the files for other genomes such as mm10. - the genome used, either the .fa file of the reference used to build bowtie2 reference (toplevel.fa for ensembl) or a string such as hg38 or mm10 if the genome was configured in homer with configureHomer.pl (GENOME) - Adaptor trimming will be realized if the R1_ADAPTOR and the R2_ADAPTORfields are present

  sequencing_1:
    SAMPLES:
      sample_1:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        TYPE: H3K27AC
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
      sample_2:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        TYPE: ATAC
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
    INPUT:
      Input_Batch1:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
    PATH: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
    R1_ADAPTOR: CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT (modify to the sequence corresponding to your samples or remove this field to not trim)
    R2_ADAPTOR: CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT (modify to the sequence corresponding to your samples or remove this field to not trim)

      CUTADAPT: -q 20 --pair-filter=any (cutadapt paramters by default, modify or leave empty)
      BOWTIE2_REF: <PATH>/index-bowtie-2.3.0/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.toplevel (modify to point to your reference for bowtie2)
      BLACKLIST_BED: <PATH>/hg38-blacklist.v2.bed 
      GENOME: <PATH>/ensembl/release-99/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.toplevel.fa
      CHROM_SIZE: <PATH>/hg38.chrom.sizes
  sequencing_2:
    SAMPLES:
      sample_3:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        TYPE: H3K27AC
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
      sample_4:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        TYPE: ATAC
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
    INPUT:
      Input_Batch2:
        R1: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
        R2: <PATH_TO_R2_fastq>
    PATH: <PATH_TO_R1_fastq>
    R1_ADAPTOR: CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT (modify to the sequence corresponding to your samples or remove this field to not trim)
    R2_ADAPTOR: CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT (modify to the sequence corresponding to your samples or remove this field to not trim)
    PARAMETERS:
      CUTADAPT: -q 20 --pair-filter=any (cutadapt paramters by default, modify or leave empty)
      BOWTIE2_REF: <PATH>/index-bowtie-2.3.0/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.toplevel (modify to point to your reference for bowtie2)
      BLACKLIST_BED: <PATH>/hg38-blacklist.v2.bed 
      GENOME: <PATH>/ensembl/release-99/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.toplevel.fa
      CHROM_SIZE: <PATH>/hg38.chrom.sizes
Basically a sequencing correspond to the samples that: - share the same trimming adaptor (if you wish to trim the fastq) - were prepared together and share the same input condition (for the ChIP-seq experiment) - they don’t necessarily share the same epigenetic information (TYPE field) but if they does, they will be rattached to the same project
In the previous the samples 1 and 2 were prepared separatelly from the samples 3 and 4. The samples 1 and 3 are from ChIP-seq experiments and need an input sample to act as background when identifying the peaks. The inputs will be the one for their respective experiments. However, the 2 sequencings may be part of a single project. Thus we use the PROJECTS field to decide which samples will be used to generate the count matrix.
PROJECTS is used to regroup samples of different sequencing when realising peak calling and the minimal number of samples in which a peak is identified to be keep in the final count matrix. To be regrouped, the samples need to shares the same mark. The path of each project indicate where the files resulting of the peak calling will be created. It is recommanded to use different folders for each projects.

  ATAC:
    PROJECT_PATH: <PATH>
    TYPE: ATAC
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 2
    SEQUENCING:
    - MO211
  ChIP_H3K27ME3:
    PROJECT_PATH: <PATH>
    TYPE: H3K27ME3
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 2
    SEQUENCING:
    - MO203
  ChIP_H3K27AC:
    PROJECT_PATH: <PATH>
    TYPE: H3K27AC
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 2
    SEQUENCING:
    - MO203
  ChIP_H2AUB:
    PROJECT_PATH: <PATH>
    TYPE: H2AUB
    MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_PEAKS: 2
    SEQUENCING:
    - MO203
Finally, he JOBS field is used to indicate the number of cpus to use for multithreadings, and the QOS and partitions to request when running jobs on a clusters with an executor like slurm.
JOBS:
  CORES_PER_JOBS:
    FASTQC: 10
    CUTADAPT: 10
    BOWTIE2: 30
  SCHEDULER_PROFILES:
    short:
      MaxWall: 1440
    medium:
      MaxWall: 4320
    long:
      MaxWall: 11520

genomake chromake -c ./config.yaml --cores 250 --local-cores 1 --jobs 8
All options can be checked with a:
genomake chromake -h

genomake chromake -c ./config.yaml --cores 250 --local-cores 1 --jobs 8 --others-snakemake "--executor slurm --default-resources slurm_account=singlecell clusters=nautilus --slurm-logdir ./logs --slurm-keep-successful-logs --slurm-delete-logfiles-older-than 0 --rerun-incomplete -np --unlock" -p
